newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bonds firm but quiet, new issues widen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bonds firm but quiet, new issues widen.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds spreads were largely unchanged at midsession with few signs of followthrough business from Friday's rally, dealers said.
High-grades sellers were equally quiet, however, and traders said the day was shaping up as a typically quiet Monday session. Market tone was intact, traders added.
"It's quiet but I think you'll find there's still cash around," one high-grades trader said. "They might sell a rally but then they'll recommit - they'll buy the back-up."
Some new issues widened substantially when freed to trade, dealers said, reflecting mispricing more than market weakness.

Travelers/Aetna's $200 million three-year A2/single-A three-year notes were quoted behind 30 basis points over U.S. Treasuries compared with the original issue spread of 25 basis points. Smith Barney Inc was lead manager on the deal.

Norwest Corp's $200 million AA3/AA-minus 10-year senior notes also sought equilibrium when freed, widening nine basis points on the bid side. The notes were quoted at 49 basis point bid, 47 offer at midday versus the original issue spread of 40 basis points.
One trader said the market also noted expectations of mounting corporate debt brought new issues "back to reality."
Leading the pack, Smith Barney Holdings is expected to issue $200 million A2/A-minus 10-year debt at a spread at or near 68 basis points over Treasuries on Monday.

Elsewhere on Friday, Dayton Hudson Corp issued $200 million in Baa1/BBB-plus five-year notes at a 54 basis point spread and International Lease Finance set $100 million A1/A-plus five-year notes at a 37.5 basis point spread.

In high-yields, prices were flat but few markets were reported as dealers sized up Friday's rally and prospects for the week. As with investment-grade debt, traders were wary of repercussions from an expected rise in new issuance.
